key_decisions.rationale: Keeps widow’s vulnerability, persistence, and legal demand.

key_decisions.after: There was also a widow in that city who kept coming to him, saying, ‘Give me justice against my opponent.’

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves divine contrast, chosen ones, continual cry, justice, and patience question.
key_decisions.before: Will God not certainly bring justice for his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night? Will he keep delaying over them?
key_decisions.after: Will God not certainly give justice to his chosen people who cry out to him day and night? Will he delay long over them?
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: And will not God certainly bring about justice for his chosen ones who cry to him day and night? Will he delay long over them?

key_decisions.rationale: Keeps assurance, speed, contrasting question, coming, and faith.
key_decisions.before: I tell you, he will bring them justice quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
key_decisions.after: I tell you, he will give them justice quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
key_decisions.tsw_comparator: I say to you that he will bring about justice for them quickly. Nevertheless, when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves ambiguous self-directed prayer, list, and contemptuous comparison.

key_decisions.tsw_comparator: The Pharisee, standing by himself, was praying these things: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like the rest of people—extortioners, unjust, adulterers, or even like this tax collector.

key_decisions.rationale: Preserves distance, lowered eyes, repeated bodily grief, and definite self-accusation.
